subject: US / EU / APAC pinning scenarios, snapshot & DR runbook
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Harding <lisa.harding@brightcarehealth.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: residency constraints + next steps

Hi Lisa — good to meet earlier, thanks for walking through BrightCare's deployment constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary (from your ask)
- Primary deployment: US-only pin (data at rest and inference residency in us-west region).
- Cross-region failover: acceptable for emergency DR only, but any failover writes must be purged/archived per your retention policy (see bullets below).
- PII handling: token-level logs should be masked for SSNs and direct identifiers; customer wants 0-7 day requestable detailed logs, 30–90 day masked aggregates.

Questions we promised to follow up on
1) Can we set a strict region pin with a cold-read backup in EU/APAC but disallow reads there except during tested DR?
2) Preferred snapshot cadence and retention for your compliance team (you mentioned quarterly snapshots as a minimum).
3) Exact retention windows for diagnostic logs vs. masked analytics you need for product telemetry.

Attachments: I attached a draft residency matrix and a short snapshot retention summary for your review.

Suggested next steps
- BrightCare to confirm snapshot retention target (e.g., 90 days encrypted snapshots, 1 year cold archive) — Lisa, can you confirm?
- Redwood to propose a failover runbook that enforces read-locks in non-pinned regions and automated purge post-failover — I'll loop in KarT to outline feasibility and ops steps.
- If acceptable, we can convert the runbook to a short SOW addendum for Dedicated/Private deployment options.

If helpful, propose a 30-minute DR-drill planning call next week — Wed/Thu morning PST open on our side.

Thanks,
Grace
--

From: Lisa Harding <lisa.harding@brightcarehealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency constraints + next steps

Thanks Grace — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Snapshot cadence: Compliance prefers weekly incremental snapshots with a full quarterly snapshot. Retention: 90 days (quick restore window) + 2 year cold archive for legal hold.
- Cross-region: We want failover reads allowed only under explicit incident code (we have an internal incident tag). Any operational reads in EU/APAC must be logged and an export of affected records produced for SOC review.
- Logs: For telemetry, 30 days raw, 180 days masked aggregates; for audit logs (access, admin actions) we need 1 year immutable retention.

We'll need an ops-level checklist to validate that non-privileged monitoring in warm backups cannot read PII. Can you confirm Redwood supports read-locks (deny-read) per region and snapshot encryption keys that we can rotate?

Also CC'd ops@brightcarehealth — they may have more detailed requirements. Happy to take the 30-min DR-drill call; Wed 10:00am PST works for us.

-Lisa
Lisa Harding
Head of Cloud Ops, BrightCare Health
lisa.harding@brightcarehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-4422
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Harding <lisa.harding@brightcarehealth.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Jun 2029 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency constraints + next steps

Appreciate the detail — that helps a lot. Quick replies inline: 

- Snapshots: We can do weekly incrementals + quarterly fulls by default. Archive to cold storage for 2 years possible as an add-on (we'll include estimated storage cost in the SOW). See attached snapshot_retention_summary.pdf for defaults and encryption options.
- Read-locks / deny-reads per region: supported. We implement region-affinity pins at the routing layer and maintain read-locks via an ops policy gate; during a failover the gate opens under a documented incident tag and we create an auditable export.
- Key rotation: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS) for snapshots in Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with rotation windows and HSM-backed options for enterprise.
- Logs: We can provide raw telemetry for 30d, masked aggregates for 180d, and immutable audit logs for 1 year (append-only). Exports for SOC review are supported via gated Playbook run.

Alex — can you draft a concise DR-drill runbook that: (a) documents the incident tag switch, (b) lists the manual gating steps and automated alerts, and (c) enumerates the purge/export tooling we will run post-failover? Aim for a 1-page playbook we can share with BrightCare before the call.

Lisa — Wed 10am PST confirmed from our side. Sending calendar invite shortly.

Best,
Grace
--
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Harding <lisa.harding@brightcarehealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Jun 2029 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency constraints + next steps (DR runbook draft)

Hi Lisa / Grace — attaching a short draft runbook and three concrete constraints we recommend for the SOW. Attachment: pinning-runbook-draft.md (outline below).

Runbook highlights (one-page summary)
- Objective: Ensure BrightCare primary reads/writes remain in us-west; EU/APAC host snapshots for DR-only with deny-read gating.
- Pre-drill checklist: snapshot success verification, KMS key status, incident tag access list, notification routing (PagerDuty + Ops Slack).
- Failover procedure (summary): 
  1) Incident declared with incident-tag: BRIGHT-FAILOVER-<id>. Ops runbook gate: Grace or BrightCare oncall toggles regional read-lock.
  2) Automated export job runs to collect affected records and audit log extract to a secure S3 bucket (encrypted with customer-managed key).
  3) Post-incident: immediate purge schedule — incremental purge of ephemeral logs within 72 hours, snapshot retention enforcement runs to mark any replicated snapshot for deletion unless legal hold exists.

Three SOW constraints we propose to include (short text for the commercial team)
- Constraint A: Region pin enforced at routing + storage replication limited to DR-archive with deny-read enforcement unless incident tag toggled.
- Constraint B: Snapshot encryption using customer-managed KMS in Dedicated/Private deployments; Hosted customers may opt for HSM-backed envelope encryption.
- Constraint C: Audit export and purge timeline commitments: export delivered within 24 hours of incident closure; purge window completed within 14 days (subject to legal hold exceptions).

Links: hubspot record and runbook draft in Drive (see metadata).

Next steps: convert the three constraints into a short SOW addendum, share costs for 2-year cold archive, and run the DR drill next Wed 10:00am PST.

-Karthik
